actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

Links: [{"title":"use stick to bottom","url":"https://docsearch.algolia.com/mcp/docs/repo/stackblitz-labs/use-stick-to-bottom"},{"title":"use stick to bottom","url":"https://bestofjs.org/projects/use-stick-to-bottom"},{"title":"TypeScript icon, indicating that this package has built-in type declarations","url":"https://npmjs.com/package/use-stick-to-bottom"},{"title":"use-stick-to-bottom  by stackblitz-labs","url":"https://www.sourcepulse.org/projects/1846316"},{"title":"download.hermesedi.duckdns.org","url":"https://download.hermesedi.duckdns.org/.hermes/hermes-agent/node_modules/use-stick-to-bottom/dist/StickToBottom.d.ts"},{"title":"# `useStickToBottom`","url":"https://download.hermesedi.duckdns.org/.hermes/hermes-agent/node_modules/use-stick-to-bottom/README.md"},{"title":"# `useStickToBottom`","url":"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/use-stick-to-bottom@1.1.6/README.md"},{"title":"vue stick to bottom","url":"https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/package/vue-stick-to-bottom"},{"title":"huggingface.co","url":"https://huggingface.co/spaces/GamerC0der/bolt.new/blob/main/app/lib/hooks/useStickToBottom.tsx"}]

The `use-stick-to-bottom` package is a React library from StackBlitz, built for AI chat interfaces such as bolt.new.

- **Purpose:** It is a zero-dependency React hook and component that keeps a container pinned to its bottom edge and smoothly adjusts as new content streams in. It is designed with AI chat bots in mind and powers bolt.new by StackBlitz.
- **API:** It exports a `<StickToBottom>` component, with a `<StickToBottom.Content>` sub-component, and a `useStickToBottom` hook for custom control. The package includes the component for declarative use and the hook for programmatic control. The context hook exposes an `isAtBottom` flag and a `scrollToBottom` function, which is useful for showing a "jump to latest" button.
- **Scroll behavior:** Users can break the stickiness by scrolling up. It uses the ResizeObserver API to detect content resizes and supports content shrinking without losing stickiness. Its animations use velocity-based springs rather than duration-based easing, which the author argues suits streamed content of variable size.
- **Browser support:** It avoids the `overflow-anchor` CSS property, which Safari does not support.
- **Install:** It is published on npm as `use-stick-to-bottom`. Install via npm: npm install use-stick-to-bottom or yarn: yarn add use-stick-to-bottom.
- **Ports:** An unofficial Vue port, `vue-stick-to-bottom`, exists. It is an unofficial port of use-stick-to-bottom.

Note that the GitHub repo (stackblitz-labs/use-stick-to-bottom) and npm page are the primary sources. Popularity figures vary across aggregators, so I didn't rely on them.

- **API:** It exports a `<StickToBottom>` component, with a `<StickToBottom.Content>` sub-component, and a `useStickToBottom` hook for custom control. The package includes the component for declarative use and the hook for programmatic control. The context hook exposes an `isAtBottom` flag and a `scrollToBottom` function, which is useful for showing a "jump to latest" button.
- **Scroll behavior:** Users can break the stickiness by scrolling up. It uses the ResizeObserver API to detect content resizes and supports content shrinking without losing stickiness. Its animations use velocity-based springs rather than duration-based easing, which the author argues suits streamed content of variable size.
- **Browser support:** It avoids the `overflow-anchor` CSS property, which Safari does not support.
- **Install:** It is published on npm as `use-stick-to-bottom`. Install via npm: npm install use-stick-to-bottom or yarn: yarn add use-stick-to-bottom.
- **Ports:** An unofficial Vue port, `vue-stick-to-bottom`, exists. It is an unofficial port of use-stick-to-bottom.

Note that the GitHub repo (stackblitz-labs/use-stick-to-bottom) and npm page are the primary sources. Popularity figures vary across aggregators, so I didn't rely on them.

The search turned up useful material on anchoring and streaming scroll behavior, but little specifically on "scroll to bottom" button design.

- **Anchoring the user's message:** The shadcn Message Scroller docs describe marking a turn's starting row as an anchor. When a new anchor arrives, the viewport places it near the top and keeps a sliver of the previous item visible so the reply doesn't feel disconnected from the prompt. An anchor is the row the viewport should treat as the start of that turn. The same docs note that anchors aren't limited to user messages. You can turn any row into an anchor, such as a system marker or a handoff event.

- **Streaming and scroll-event problems:** A Medium post describes a common bug. Content grows token by token, so the browser fires scroll events without any user input, and an auto-scroll handler mistakes this for the user scrolling away. The author's fix was to treat only real wheel or trackpad input as user intent, and to add bottom padding so the maximum scroll distance lines up correctly. Every time a new token came in and the message grew taller, the browser would fire a scroll event, which froze the view mid-response.

- **Virtualized lists:** TanStack Virtual's chat guide recommends end anchoring and following new output only when the user is already at the latest item. Its example config includes followOnAppend: true and a scrollEndThreshold of 80. That threshold is the mechanism that decides whether the user is "near the bottom," which is the same condition that should govern when a "scroll to bottom" button appears.

- **Gap:** None of the results describe the button itself (when it appears, its placement, or how it behaves during streaming). The closest is the implied pattern: show the button when the user is not near the bottom, and hide it when they return. Further searching would be needed to confirm current design conventions.

**`useStickToBottom`** is a zero-dependency React hook and component that keeps a scrollable container pinned to its bottom edge. It is "Designed with AI chat bots in mind," and it smooths the view as streamed content arrives.

- **Resize handling:** Scroll anchoring is handled so that resizing content above the viewport doesn't make the visible content jump.

**Summary:** The page describes a `MessageScroller` component with follow-output, turn anchoring, and a scroll-to-end control. It does not specify a "new messages" indicator, a button label or placement, pixel thresholds for the live edge, or any comparison to ChatGPT or Claude.

**When the user sends a message (anchor)**
- Marking a row with `scrollAnchor` makes it the start of a turn. The docs say that "When a new anchor is appended, the viewport moves it near the top."
- A peek of the previous item stays visible above it. `scrollPreviousItemPeek` "keeps a slice of the previous item visible above the anchor." The example uses 64px. No default is given.
- Anchoring is not tied to role. Any row can anchor, such as a user message or a marker.

**While a reply streams**
- With `autoScroll` enabled, "`autoScroll` keeps streamed replies in view as they grow."
- Anchoring and follow-output work together. The view "stays put while the reply streams into the room below it." Once the reply fills the viewport, "follow-output takes over from the anchor."

**When the user scrolls up**
- Leaving the live edge stops following. The docs say that "Scrolling away from the live edge releases the view, whether by wheel, touch, keyboard scroll keys, or dragging the scrollbar."
- An explicit message jump also releases following.
- New chunks then arrive without moving the reader.
- The docs do not define how close to the bottom counts as "at the live edge." No threshold is given.

**Scroll-to-end control**
- `MessageScrollerButton` "Scrolls to the start or end of the transcript and is inert until there is content in its direction."
- It is not described as appearing or disappearing. Instead, when there is nothing to scroll toward, it sets `inert`, uses `tabIndex={-1}`, and exposes `data-active="false"`.
- Calling `scrollToEnd` or pressing the button "re-engages follow-output when `autoScroll` is enabled."
- While that programmatic scroll runs, the root and viewport expose `data-autoscrolling`.
- The page does not specify the button's label or placement. The demos render "Scroll to end," but the API text does not define it.

**"New messages" indicator**
- The component does not define one. The "Jump to latest" action and showing out-of-view streaming appear only as general recommendations in the "What Makes a Great Streaming Chat Experience" section.

**Thresholds**
- The only numeric values are the 64px peek example and the 125-character-free prose. No live-edge tolerance, scroll-away distance, or button-visibility threshold is documented.

**ChatGPT or Claude comparison**
- The page does not mention ChatGPT or Claude. It describes its goals in general terms, such as "Auto-scroll should never be the default."

The search didn't turn up anything official about how claude.ai handles scrolling during streaming, and nothing that mentions a "scroll to bottom" arrow on claude.ai. The results are mostly user bug reports and feature requests about Claude Code, so they show the intended behavior and known problems rather than the current web UI.

- **Scroll jumping during streaming:** One report describes the Claude Code Desktop app on Windows force-scrolling to the bottom on every streamed update, even after the user scrolled up. The reporter says this is the same UX that was already shipped for the VSCode extension via issue #11092, and that the desktop app appears to be missing that fix (or has regressed it). That report is marked as resolved.
- **Snapping to the top:** Several other reports describe scrolling during a stream snapping the view to the top of the conversation instead of holding position. One says scrolling up during streaming should either hold the current scroll position or, at most, snap back to the bottom. These are also marked resolved.
- **Expected "sticky bottom" behavior:** The reports describe the standard pattern: if the user is at the bottom of the scroll container, auto-scroll to follow new streaming content, and if the user has scrolled up beyond that threshold, do NOT auto-scroll. Some suggest a "jump to bottom" button / new-message indicator as an optional addition.
- **Keeping the prompt visible:** A feature request asked to pin the user's prompt message at the top of the viewport while scrolling through Claude's response. It was closed on the day it was opened, and the results don't say whether it was implemented.

Overall, the results suggest that auto-scroll pausing when the user scrolls up, plus a jump-to-bottom control, is the intended behavior, and that it has regressed at times in some clients. I couldn't confirm the current claude.ai web behavior or the arrow button from these results. Checking Anthropic's release notes or help center would be the next step.

**Why auto-scroll should not be the default**

The guidance ties this to the reader's control over the view. Under "Move only when the reader asked to move," it says: "Auto-scroll should never be the default." The principle is that the interface should only move when the reader has asked it to, so the reader is never pulled away from what they're reading.

**Following only while the reader is at the live edge**

The page says: "Follow only while they're following." Staying at the live edge keeps the stream in view. Scrolling away leaves the reader where they are.

**Streaming content out of view**

The page says: "The conversation can keep streaming without changing what the reader is looking at." New content can arrive offscreen without moving the view.

**Indicating streaming and new messages**

Under "Show what's happening out of view," the page says: "Make it clear when a response is still streaming or when new messages have arrived." The interface should signal activity the reader can't currently see.

**Jump to latest**

Under "Make it easy to return to the latest reply," the page says: "A "Jump to latest" action should bring the reader back and resume following." The Virtualization and Following sections add that calling `scrollToEnd` or pressing `MessageScrollerButton` re-engages follow-output when `autoScroll` is enabled.

**Unread indicators**

The page mentions unread markers only briefly, in the navigation guidance: "Long threads need message links, search, unread markers, and direct navigation." It does not describe how to implement them.

content.content:
**Initial position:** On mount, the list scrolls to the bottom. This is controlled by `shouldScrollToBottom`, which defaults to `true`. Setting it to `false` disables the initial scroll.

**Submitted messages:** When a user message is submitted, it is scrolled to the top of the viewport. The last message's minimum height is then adjusted dynamically using a `--last-message-height` CSS variable, so the message can sit at the top while the reply has room to appear. The docs don't explain how that height is calculated.

**Following streaming:** Continuous scrolling as messages arrive is controlled by `shouldAutoScroll`, which defaults to `false`. The overview lists auto-scrolling during streaming as a feature, but the prop reference says it's off by default, so you must enable it explicitly.

**Auto scroll button:**
- **Appearance:** It appears when the user scrolls up, and clicking it returns to the latest messages.
- **Prop (`autoScroll`):** Accepts `true` (default), `false` to hide the button, or a Button props object. Defaults are `size: 'md'`, `color: 'neutral'`, and `variant: 'outline'`.
- **Placement:** The theme positions it absolutely, horizontally centered, at the bottom of its container, with a rounded-full shape. The viewport wrapper uses `top-[86%]`.
- **Icon (`autoScrollIcon`):** Defaults to the app's `arrowDown` icon (`i-lucide-arrow-down` in the examples). Override it per instance, or globally via `ui.icons.arrowDown` in `app.config.ts` (Nuxt) or `vite.config.ts` (Vue).

**Sticky footer:** With the `#footer` slot, the footer's height is measured, so the last message keeps enough space and the button stays above the prompt. For a prompt outside the scroll container (e.g., in a DashboardPanel or Sidebar), the docs suggest `ui: { viewport: 'sticky top-auto bottom-4 h-0' }`. # Agent pane scrolling: what is wrong, what everyone else does, and two decisions

Untracked working note, 2026-10-28, revised after looking at how other AI chat
UIs handle this. Branch `claude/chat-scroll` (cut from origin/jusprin-newui
434e893a6b, nothing changed yet).

## What happened in the walkthrough, and why

The pane follows new content only while the reader is within 24 px of the
bottom. Scrolling up anywhere switches following off, and only scrolling back
down switches it on again (`MessageList.tsx`, `followBottom`). Nothing else
resets it, including the person's own message.

The walkthrough scrolled up to read the plan (frame 1B-06, "The plan,
scrolled up"). The pane then stayed parked through the ABS change and the
manual slice (2C-03 shows the same position), so the question "Is it still
fine to print like this?" and its answer were added below the fold. Nothing
on screen said they existed.

Reproduced in the built page with a fake host (340 × 720 window, 413 px of
thread):

| Trigger | At the bottom | Scrolled up |
|---|---|---|
| The person sends a message | follows | **stays put; the message lands 419 px below the view** |
| Same, from only 40 px above the bottom | | **stays put; message 88 px below** |
| Agent answer streaming | follows every word | stays put |
| App-started turn (a slice ends, the agent reports) | follows | stays put |

Screenshot of the stuck state:
`/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-priceless-napier-147653/e205b652-5d1b-44cc-aa1e-2a1afbfd5940/scratchpad/repro-send-while-held.jpg`

Also found: typing several lines grows the composer, which then covers the
last 100 px of the thread even at the bottom, because the thread getting
shorter does not count as a reason to follow.

## What the established chat UIs do

I looked at the chat components that AI products are built from. They all
publish their scroll behaviour, which the products themselves do not:

- **use-stick-to-bottom** (StackBlitz; runs bolt.new, and Vercel's AI
  Elements `Conversation` is built on it): follows the bottom; a scroll up by
  the person releases it; content that grows or shrinks, including a resize,
  never releases it. A round down-arrow button, centred at the bottom of the
  thread, shows whenever the view is not at the bottom and scrolls there.
- **Vercel AI Elements**: `ConversationScrollButton` "appears when the user
  has scrolled up, allowing them to return to the bottom."
- **assistant-ui**: two modes. The default, "bottom", is classic chat that
  scrolls to the bottom when a run starts. "top" places the new user message
  at the top of the viewport and does not follow the answer.
- **Nuxt UI ChatMessages**: a sent message is scrolled to the top of the
  viewport, and the space under it is reserved so it can stay there while the
  reply arrives. Following the stream is off by default. A round, outlined
  `arrow-down` button, centred above the prompt, appears when scrolled up.
- **shadcn Message Scroller**: the sent message moves "near the top", with a
  slice of the previous item still visible above it, and the reply streams
  into the room below. Scrolling away by wheel, touch, keys or the scrollbar
  releases following. Its jump button "brings the reader back and resumes
  following". Its guidance: "Follow only while they're following."
- **ChatGPT**: no first-party description. A feature request from August 2026
  says it follows a long answer to its end, and that the poster has to scroll
  back several screens to find where it started. They ask for exactly the
  "top" behaviour plus a "↓ Jump to latest" button. Users describe a small
  down arrow that appears when scrolled up.

Where they all agree:

1. **Sending always moves the view to the person's message.** Some go to the
   bottom, some put the message at the top, but none leaves it off-screen.
   Ours does; that is the bug.
2. A scroll up by the person stops following. New content never moves a
   reader who has scrolled away.
3. **One plain down-arrow button, centred just above the composer**, shown
   only while the view is not at the bottom. None of them uses a label, a
   count or an edge shadow.
4. The button lands at the bottom and following resumes.
5. Following survives size changes, so the composer growing keeps the bottom
   in view.

## Changes from my first proposal

- Dropped the "New reply" label, the shadow above the composer and the "jump
  to the start of the newest turn" landing. None of the reference designs
  does them. The button is plain and lands at the bottom (points 3 and 4).
- Kept "bring the message to the top" as an option, because three of the five
  components ship it and the ChatGPT request asks for it. It is no longer the
  only answer: "scroll to the bottom and follow" is just as standard.

## Decision 1: where the person's sent message lands

**1A. At the bottom; the answer is followed as it streams.** This is
use-stick-to-bottom, AI Elements and assistant-ui's default, and what ChatGPT
reportedly does. It is the smallest change: it only adds "a new message from
the person scrolls to the bottom and follows" to today's code. The cost is
that a long answer ends on its last line, and the person scrolls up to find
its start. That is what made the walkthrough scroll up to read the plan.

**1B. Near the top, with a peek of the previous item; the answer fills in
below it and the view then holds.** (Recommended.) This is Nuxt UI,
assistant-ui "top" and shadcn, and it is what the ChatGPT request asks for.
The person starts reading their question and the top of the answer; the rest
is one press of the arrow away. It needs room reserved under the last turn
so the message can sit at the top while the answer is still short.

Either way, "sent" means any new message from the person, including Ask AI
from the issue chip and a tapped reply choice. Answers and app-started turns
never move a reader who has scrolled away.

## Decision 2: the jump button's shape

Every reference design uses a **circle**. Our design system reserves the
`full` radius for the reply choice ("the one capsule control"), and its own
icon button is a 32 DIP square with the 4 DIP radius.

**2A. A 32 DIP circle**, `surface.canvas` with a `border.subtle` stroke and
`elevation.subtle`, Lucide `arrow-down`. It matches what people already know,
and needs a sentence in the design-system doc that allows the full radius on
this one icon button. (Recommended.)

**2B. The design system's 32 DIP icon button (4 DIP radius)**, same fill,
stroke, shadow and icon. It needs no doc change, but looks unlike the control
people know from other chat apps.

Either way it is centred 8 DIP above the composer box and floats over the
thread. `arrow-down` gets pinned next to the `arrow-up` already in
`resources/jusprin/ui/icons`. No new tokens are needed.

## How to build it: borrow, don't rewrite

`use-stick-to-bottom` 1.1.6 is MIT, has no dependencies, and supports React
18. It already handles the hard parts: telling the person's scroll from
content growth, resizes (which fixes the composer bug), and keeping the view
still when content above it changes. It has a `targetScrollTop` option for a
scroll target other than the very bottom, which is how 1B would place the
message at the top. I'd recommend adopting it in place of the hand-written
`followBottom` logic, unless you would rather not add a dependency to the
page. In that case the same rules are about 60 lines of our own code.

# Agent pane scrolling: what is wrong and three decisions for Kenneth

Untracked working note, 2026-10-28. Branch `claude/chat-scroll` (cut from
origin/jusprin-newui 434e893a6b, nothing changed yet).

## What happened in the walkthrough, and why

The pane follows new content only while the reader is within 24 px of the
bottom. Scrolling up anywhere switches following off, and only scrolling back
down switches it on again (`MessageList.tsx`, `followBottom`). Nothing else
resets it: not the person's own message.

The walkthrough scrolled up to read the plan (frame 1B-06 says "The plan,
scrolled up"). The pane then stayed parked there through the ABS change and
the manual slice (2C-03 shows the same scroll position), so when the question
"Is it still fine to print like this?" was sent, both it and the answer were
added below the fold. Nothing on screen said they existed.

Reproduced in the built page with a fake host (340 × 720 window, 413 px of
thread). Each case below is "where the reader was" → "what the pane did":

| Trigger | At the bottom | Scrolled up |
|---|---|---|
| The person sends a message | follows | **stays put; the message lands 419 px below the view** |
| Same, but only 40 px above the bottom | | **stays put; message 88 px below** |
| Agent answer streaming | follows every word | stays put |
| App-started turn (a slice ends, then the agent reports) | follows | stays put |
| A slice card starts | follows | stays put |

Screenshot of the stuck state:
`/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-priceless-napier-147653/e205b652-5d1b-44cc-aa1e-2a1afbfd5940/scratchpad/repro-send-while-held.jpg`

So there are two defects: the person's own message does not override "hold",
and when the pane holds, nothing shows that something new is below.

Found on the way: when the person types several lines, the composer grows and
covers the last 100 px of the thread, even at the bottom, because a change in
the thread's height does not count as new content. Same rule, same fix; I
would fix it in this change unless you say otherwise.

## The design system today

- The pinned setup card already has an edge rule: while the thread is
  scrolled under it, the card gets the `elevation.subtle` shadow below its
  divider. The bottom edge (above the composer) has no matching rule.
- The `full` radius is reserved: the reply choice is "the one capsule
  control". A floating "New reply" pill in capsule form would break that, so
  the options below use the existing 4 DIP button shapes.
- The closest floating control in the app is the canvas's "N print issues"
  button at the canvas's bottom edge.

## Decision 1: what a sent message does

**1A. Jump to the bottom and follow.** Today's behaviour, applied even after
scrolling up. Simple. But a long answer streams past the top of the view, and
the person ends at its last line and has to scroll up to read its start. That
is how the walkthrough came to scroll up in the first place.

**1B. Bring the person's message to the top of the pane, then hold.**
(Recommended.) The answer streams in below the question and the view stops
moving once the turn fills the pane; the reader starts at the top of the
answer. The rest shows through the jump control below. Claude.ai and ChatGPT
work roughly this way.

Either way, "sent" means any new message from the person, so Ask AI from the
issue chip and tapping a reply choice count too. Answers and app-started turns
that arrive while the person is scrolled up never move the view.

## Decision 2: how the pane says there is more below

**2A. A jump button only.** (Recommended.) It appears whenever the bottom of
the thread is out of view. It's a 32 DIP icon button (`button.icon`, Lucide
`arrow-down`, which would be pinned next to the `arrow-up` already in
`resources/jusprin/ui/icons`; the pinned `chevron-down` also works) on `surface.canvas`, with a `border.subtle` stroke and
`elevation.subtle`, centred 8 DIP above the composer box. Pressing it is
decision 3.

**2B. 2A, plus a label when something is new.** If a reply or report arrived
while the person was scrolled up, the button becomes "New reply" with the
arrow (`button.secondarySmall`, 28 DIP), and goes back to the plain arrow once
seen. This tells someone reading the plan that the agent has said something.
It costs one more state to test.

**2C. 2A or 2B, plus a shadow above the composer.** This matches the setup
card's top-edge shadow at the bottom edge. It's cheap and consistent. On its
own it is too quiet to say that a new answer arrived.

I would not use a count ("2 new"). A turn can be a message, a slice card and
change rows, so the number would not match what the person sees.

## Decision 3: where the jump lands

**3A. At the bottom,** and following resumes.

**3B. At the start of the newest turn when that turn is taller than the pane,
otherwise at the bottom.** (Recommended, and needed if you choose 1B.) The
person lands on their question with the answer under it, not on the answer's
last line.

## My recommendation in one line

1B + 2B + 3B, plus the composer-growth fix: the person's message always comes
into view at the top, answers never pull the view away, and a single arrow
button (labelled "New reply" when something arrived) jumps to the newest turn.
It needs no new tokens, only the one pinned icon. I would draw boards on the canvas only if you want to
see 2B's two states before I build it.

# Agent pane scrolling: what is wrong, what everyone else does, and two decisions

Untracked working note, 2026-10-28, revised after looking at how other AI chat
UIs handle this. Branch `claude/chat-scroll` (cut from origin/jusprin-newui
434e893a6b, nothing changed yet).

## What happened in the walkthrough, and why

The pane follows new content only while the reader is within 24 px of the
bottom. Scrolling up anywhere switches following off, and only scrolling back
down switches it on again (`MessageList.tsx`, `followBottom`). Nothing else
resets it, including the person's own message.

The walkthrough scrolled up to read the plan (frame 1B-06, "The plan,
scrolled up"). The pane then stayed parked through the ABS change and the
manual slice (2C-03 shows the same position), so the question "Is it still
fine to print like this?" and its answer were added below the fold. Nothing
on screen said they existed.

Reproduced in the built page with a fake host (340 × 720 window, 413 px of
thread):

| Trigger | At the bottom | Scrolled up |
|---|---|---|
| The person sends a message | follows | **stays put; the message lands 419 px below the view** |
| Same, from only 40 px above the bottom | | **stays put; message 88 px below** |
| Agent answer streaming | follows every word | stays put |
| App-started turn (a slice ends, the agent reports) | follows | stays put |

Screenshot of the stuck state:
`/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-priceless-napier-147653/e205b652-5d1b-44cc-aa1e-2a1afbfd5940/scratchpad/repro-send-while-held.jpg`

Also found: typing several lines grows the composer, which then covers the
last 100 px of the thread even at the bottom, because the thread getting
shorter does not count as a reason to follow.

## What the established chat UIs do

I looked at the chat components that AI products are built from. They all
publish their scroll behaviour, which the products themselves do not:

- **use-stick-to-bottom** (StackBlitz; runs bolt.new, and Vercel's AI
  Elements `Conversation` is built on it): follows the bottom; a scroll up by
  the person releases it; content that grows or shrinks, including a resize,
  never releases it. A round down-arrow button, centred at the bottom of the
  thread, shows whenever the view is not at the bottom and scrolls there.
- **Vercel AI Elements**: `ConversationScrollButton` "appears when the user
  has scrolled up, allowing them to return to the bottom."
- **assistant-ui**: two modes. The default, "bottom", is classic chat that
  scrolls to the bottom when a run starts. "top" places the new user message
  at the top of the viewport and does not follow the answer.
- **Nuxt UI ChatMessages**: a sent message is scrolled to the top of the
  viewport, and the space under it is reserved so it can stay there while the
  reply arrives. Following the stream is off by default. A round, outlined
  `arrow-down` button, centred above the prompt, appears when scrolled up.
- **shadcn Message Scroller**: the sent message moves "near the top", with a
  slice of the previous item still visible above it, and the reply streams
  into the room below. Scrolling away by wheel, touch, keys or the scrollbar
  releases following. Its jump button "brings the reader back and resumes
  following". Its guidance: "Follow only while they're following."
- **ChatGPT**: no first-party description. A feature request from August 2026
  says it follows a long answer to its end, and that the poster has to scroll
  back several screens to find where it started. They ask for exactly the
  "top" behaviour plus a "↓ Jump to latest" button. Users describe a small
  down arrow that appears when scrolled up.

Where they all agree:

1. **Sending always moves the view to the person's message.** Some go to the
   bottom, some put the message at the top, but none leaves it off-screen.
   Ours does; that is the bug.
2. A scroll up by the person stops following. New content never moves a
   reader who has scrolled away.
3. **One plain down-arrow button, centred just above the composer**, shown
   only while the view is not at the bottom. None of them uses a label, a
   count or an edge shadow.
4. The button lands at the bottom and following resumes.
5. Following survives size changes, so the composer growing keeps the bottom
   in view.

## Changes from my first proposal

- Dropped the "New reply" label, the shadow above the composer and the "jump
  to the start of the newest turn" landing. None of the reference designs
  does them. The button is plain and lands at the bottom (points 3 and 4).
- Kept "bring the message to the top" as an option, because three of the five
  components ship it and the ChatGPT request asks for it. It is no longer the
  only answer: "scroll to the bottom and follow" is just as standard.

## Decision 1: where the person's sent message lands

**1A. At the bottom; the answer is followed as it streams.** This is
use-stick-to-bottom, AI Elements and assistant-ui's default, and what ChatGPT
reportedly does. It is the smallest change: it only adds "a new message from
the person scrolls to the bottom and follows" to today's code. The cost is
that a long answer ends on its last line, and the person scrolls up to find
its start. That is what made the walkthrough scroll up to read the plan.

**1B. Near the top, with a peek of the previous item; the answer fills in
below it and the view then holds.** (Recommended.) This is Nuxt UI,
assistant-ui "top" and shadcn, and it is what the ChatGPT request asks for.
The person starts reading their question and the top of the answer; the rest
is one press of the arrow away. It needs room reserved under the last turn
so the message can sit at the top while the answer is still short.

Either way, "sent" means any new message from the person, including Ask AI
from the issue chip and a tapped reply choice. Answers and app-started turns
never move a reader who has scrolled away.

## Decision 2: the jump button's shape

Every reference design uses a **circle**. Our design system reserves the
`full` radius for the reply choice ("the one capsule control"), and its own
icon button is a 32 DIP square with the 4 DIP radius.

**2A. A 32 DIP circle**, `surface.canvas` with a `border.subtle` stroke and
`elevation.subtle`, Lucide `arrow-down`. It matches what people already know,
and needs a sentence in the design-system doc that allows the full radius on
this one icon button. (Recommended.)

**2B. The design system's 32 DIP icon button (4 DIP radius)**, same fill,
stroke, shadow and icon. It needs no doc change, but looks unlike the control
people know from other chat apps.

Either way it is centred 8 DIP above the composer box and floats over the
thread. `arrow-down` gets pinned next to the `arrow-up` already in
`resources/jusprin/ui/icons`. No new tokens are needed.

## How to build it: borrow, don't rewrite

`use-stick-to-bottom` 1.1.6 is MIT, has no dependencies, and supports React
18. It already handles the hard parts: telling the person's scroll from
content growth, resizes (which fixes the composer bug), and keeping the view
still when content above it changes. It has a `targetScrollTop` option for a
scroll target other than the very bottom, which is how 1B would place the
message at the top. I'd recommend adopting it in place of the hand-written
`followBottom` logic, unless you would rather not add a dependency to the
page. In that case the same rules are about 60 lines of our own code.

I've rewritten [chat-scroll-options.md](chat-scroll-options.md) to follow them. The diagnosis stands: once the person scrolls up, the pane stops following, and their own sent message doesn't bring it back.

**What the established designs agree on.** I looked at use-stick-to-bottom (by StackBlitz, the base of Vercel's AI Elements), assistant-ui, Nuxt UI, shadcn's Message Scroller, and what users report about ChatGPT:
1. **Sending always moves the view to the person's message.** None of them leaves it off-screen, which is exactly what ours does.
2. **Scrolling up stops following.** After that, a streaming answer or other new content never moves the reader.
3. **One plain round down-arrow button, centred just above the message box.** It shows only while the view isn't at the bottom. None of them uses a label, a count or an edge shadow.
4. **Pressing it goes to the bottom,** and following starts again.
5. **Following survives size changes.** That also fixes our second problem, where a growing message box covers the end of the thread.

**What I dropped:** the "New reply" label, the shadow above the message box, and landing the jump on the newest turn instead of the bottom.

**Two decisions left for you:**
- **Where a sent message lands.**
  - Scroll to the bottom and follow the answer as it streams. This is use-stick-to-bottom, AI Elements and assistant-ui's default.
  - Or put the message near the top and let the answer fill in below it. This is Nuxt UI, shadcn and assistant-ui's "top" mode. It's also what an August 2026 ChatGPT feature request asks for, because following a long answer leaves you on its last line. That's why the walkthrough had to scroll up to read the plan.
  - I recommend the top placement.
- **The button's shape.** Every reference uses a circle. Our design system reserves the fully round shape for reply choices, and its own icon button has 4 DIP corners. I recommend the circle plus one sentence in the design-system doc allowing it.

**How to build it:** I'd rather adopt `use-stick-to-bottom` than keep our own hand-written follow logic. It's MIT-licensed, has no dependencies and supports our React version. It already handles telling the person's scrolling apart from growing content, and resizes. It also has an option to aim the scroll somewhere other than the very bottom, which the top placement needs. If you'd rather not add a dependency to the page, the same rules are about 60 lines of our own code.

Sources:
- [use-stick-to-bottom README](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/use-stick-to-bottom@1.1.6/README.md)
- [shadcn Message Scroller](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/message-scroller)
- [Nuxt UI ChatMessages](https://ui.nuxt.com/docs/components/chat-messages)
- [assistant-ui ThreadViewport source](https://download.hermesedi.duckdns.org/.hermes/hermes-agent/node_modules/@assistant-ui/react/src/primitives/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx) (from a third-party mirror)
- [Vercel AI Elements](https://vercel.com/academy/ai-sdk/ai-elements)
- [ConversationScrollButton usage](https://aisdkagents.com/docs/ai/ai-elements)
- [OpenAI feature request on auto-scrolling](https://community.openai.com/t/feature-request-smarter-auto-scrolling-for-long-chatgpt-responses/1389613)
- [Claude Code issue citing ChatGPT's arrow](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/35261)
- [TanStack Virtual chat guide](https://tanstack.com/virtual/latest/docs/chat)
